total.description: Total number of matching ontology nodes before the limit is applied.

census.description: Whole-vault kind counts, unaffected by the filters and the page.

referencedOnlyTotal.description: Names used only in a relation, with no file of their own.

returned.description: Number of rows returned in this page.

limited.description: True when this page does not contain every matching row.

vaultRoot.description: Resolved vault root path used for the listing.

filter.description: The `filter` as sent; only with a filter.

parsedAs.description: The filter as the server read it; only with a filter.

query.description: The `mentions` text as sent; only with mentions.

uid.description: Permanent immutable node identity. Slug remains the current human-readable address.

isNode.description: Only with `mentions`. False for a plain Markdown page that lives beside the nodes: it has no `uid` or `kind` and is not part of the graph.

matchedIn.description: Only with `mentions`: where the text was found.

excerpt.description: Only with `mentions`: the first prose of the body, at most 200 characters.

excerptTruncated.description: Only present (and always true) when the body carries more than this excerpt shows, possibly the matched text.

bodyChars.description: Only alongside excerptTruncated: the full body length.

summaryTruncated.description: Only present (and always true) when the body carries more than this summary shows.

summaryHint.description: Only present when at least one row carries a partial summary — names the follow-up call that returns the full bodies.

nonNodeHint.description: Only with `mentions`, when a row is a plain Markdown page: says so and how to see nodes only.

excerptHint.description: Only with `mentions`, when a row carries a partial excerpt: names the call that returns the full bodies.

growthHint.description: Only on zero rows from `filter` or `mentions`: why nothing matched, the nearest titles to check, and the call to try next.

excerpt.description: First prose paragraph. Present only when `body` is `excerpt` (the default).

body.description: Entire markdown body. Present only when the caller passed `body: "full"`.

totalChars.description: Full markdown body length in characters.

returnedChars.description: Characters actually returned in this response.

truncated.description: True when part of the body was not returned.

hint.description: Only present when truncated — the exact call that returns the rest.

bodyInfo.description: How much of the body this response carries — always present, so truncation is never silent.

rationale.description: One-line rationale stored with this relation in the source document's `relation_notes` map (written by the `why` of an `add_relations` row). Omitted when no note is stored for the target.

ok.description: True for resolved concept rows; false for missing or invalid input rows.

uid.description: Canonical permanent UID for successful rows; requested UID for UID-selector error rows.

slug.description: Canonical slug for successful rows; the original input value for invalid partial rows.

frontmatter.description: Resolved markdown frontmatter for successful rows.

excerpt.description: First prose paragraph — successful rows in `excerpt` mode (the default).

body.description: Entire markdown body — successful rows in `full` mode.

totalChars.description: Full markdown body length in characters.

returnedChars.description: Characters actually returned in this response.

truncated.description: True when part of the body was not returned.

hint.description: Only present when truncated — the exact call that returns the rest.

neighbors.description: Direct graph neighbor buckets for successful rows.

rationale.description: One-line rationale stored with this relation in the source document's `relation_notes` map (written by the `why` of an `add_relations` row). Omitted when no note is stored for the target.

inferredFrom.description: What named the folder when `rootPath` was omitted.

status.description: The source receipt's state. The receipt itself stays in the vault sidecar.

witnessSummary.description: How many of the project's declared `path:` claims the folder holds: `supported` of `total`.

status.description: The source receipt's state. The receipt itself stays in the vault sidecar.

coverage.description: Only what the batch changed in the build depth: `changed` maps a count (`abilities.unplaced`, `areas.notMapped`, `reads.unread`, `rules.uncited`, `roles.unplaced`, `abilityEdges.capabilitiesWithoutEdge`) to `[before, after]`, and `nextAction` is the one call that moves the first count that is not zero. `validate_vault` lists the unplaced abilities.

previewReady.description: True only when this response is a complete dry-run preview that an agent can review.

canConfirm.description: True only when repeating the call with confirm:true can perform the previewed change without another explicit safety opt-in.

wouldChange.description: True only when the dry-run predicts a disk or Git change.

blockedReasons.description: Machine-readable human explanations for every condition currently blocking confirmation.

postWriteMaintenance.description: What the write leaves to do about the nodes it touched, and only them. The whole vault's queue is `validate_vault` and `query_ontology({operation:"maintenance_plan"})`.

why.description: One-line rationale ("A leans on B because ..."), stored in relation_notes in the same write. Required for a new depends_on.

nextAction.description: The step to take next about the touched nodes: the first one a call settles (`proposedAction`), else the first judgement left; null when there is none.

stepsAboutTouched.description: How many steps the maintenance plan has about the touched nodes.

findings.description: One line per kind of maintenance finding on the nodes this call wrote: the first finding with the call that settles it, then the other nodes it applies to.

uid.description: The referring node's permanent UID. Absent when that node has no valid `uid:` (validate_vault reports it) and on every non-node row.

isNode.description: True when the referrer is a graph node (has `kind:`). False for a wiki page or other Markdown that links to the target; such a row carries neither `uid` nor `kind`.

rationale.description: One-line rationale stored with this relation in the source document's `relation_notes` map (written by the `why` of an `add_relations` row). Omitted when no note is stored for the target.

growthHint.description: Only present when found=false — a candidate add_relation (both endpoints exist) or add_concept (an endpoint is missing) suggestion, derived from the real vault, not invented.

total.description: Total number of vault docs that declare a kind.

byKind.description: Node counts keyed by frontmatter kind.

referencedOnlyTotal.description: Number of slugs referenced by graph relations without a corresponding node document.

conceptsIncludingReferenced.description: Documented nodes plus referenced-only slugs, matching the graph-visible concept census.

skippedNonNodeCount.description: Summary answers only: `.md` files passed over for having no `kind:`.

delivery.description: Present when no argument asked for arrays: this is the bounded summary, and these arguments return the rest.

rationale.description: One-line rationale stored with this relation in the source document's `relation_notes` map (written by the `why` of an `add_relations` row). Omitted when no note is stored for the target.

coverage.description: Build depth as counts: `abilities` the survey lists by where each sits, `areas` mapped, `reads` of capability entry files, `rules` citing no read lines, `roles` with no element, `abilityEdges`; the page of `unplaced` abilities from `unplacedOffset`; and one `nextAction`.

unplaced.description: Up to 10 abilities no node covers, from `unplacedOffset.offset`.

unplacedOffset.description: The cursor over `unplaced`; pass `nextOffset` as `unplacedOffset` until `hasMore` is false. It is not `problemsPagination`.

nextAction.description: The one call that moves the first count that is not zero.

finalizeGate.description: What `finalize_project_meaning` refuses for a row answered `answered` and for the Not mapped yet lines, one entry per block with its count; empty when it would refuse nothing. Present when the repository is grounded.

scanned.description: Number of vault markdown files scanned.

problemsPagination.description: The page `problems` holds: `total` problem files, and `nextOffset` for the next page until `hasMore` is false.

problemsHint.description: Present when the vault has more than one page: which files this page shows and the call for the next one.

remedy.description: What to do about every issue of this code, with `<slug>` for the node. An issue without it carries its own repair.

files.description: At most 20 files with this code that are not on this page of `problems`, in page order.

filesOmitted.description: Present when `files` names fewer than `count`: how many more. Page through `problems` for them.

pathDrift.description: Vault→code path drift: frontmatter source paths missing on disk, resolved against repoRoot.

checked.description: False when the repository this vault describes could not be determined (vault outside any git repo and no repoRoot given). Then `drifts` is empty because nothing was measured — NOT because nothing drifted.

suggestedPath.description: Reconcile hint (Track A #3): a unique existing repo file sharing the missing file's basename — likely where the source moved. Present only on a unique match.

evidenceDrift.description: Whether each concept still stands on the code it cites, dated by one Git walk: current / stale / missing / unknown per concept, with the first 10 stale, missing and folder-only rows named; `omitted` counts the rest.

reason.description: Why nothing was dated, when `checked` is false.

folderOnly.description: Unknown rows whose only moved evidence is a folder path.
Concepts whose only evidence that moved is a folder: something under it changed, which is not yet a verdict on the meaning.

omitted.description: How many rows were cut from `stale`, `missing` and `folderOnly`, by group.

pageCount.description: Pages judged: the whole folder, or the named `paths`.

failingCount.description: Pages with at least one problem. Zero means every page judged fits.

pagination.description: The page `pages` holds: `offset` is its position among `total` failing pages and `nextOffset` the position after it, both as of this call; resume with `nextCall`. Absent with `paths`.

nextCall.description: Present while more failing pages remain: the exact call for the next page.

pagesHint.description: Present when the failing pages span more than one reply: which ones this reply shows, why it stopped, and the next call.

summary.description: The whole folder, whatever page `pages` holds. Absent with `paths`.

blockingPages.description: Failing pages with at least one problem that is not advisory.

advisoryOnlyPages.description: Failing pages whose only problems are advisory (orphan-page, shared-source-unlinked).

severity.description: `warning` for an advisory code, `error` for the rest.

files.description: At most 20 of the `count` pages with this code, blocking pages first, each group by path.

filesOmitted.description: Present when `files` names fewer than `count`: how many more. Page through `pages` for them.

pages.description: Without `paths`, failing pages only, one page of them. With `paths`, every named page.

blocking.description: Whether any problem is more than advisory (orphan-page and shared-source-unlinked are advisory).

detail.description: The pieces of `message`, so a screen can retell it in the reader's language: `key` names the sentence, `values` fills it.

problems.description: At most 20, in the order judged; each message escapes control and format characters.

problemsOmitted.description: Present when the page has more problems than `problems` shows: how many more.

reason.description: Why the import could not resolve. `empty` may have an empty spec; other reasons preserve the original import spec.

kindCounts.description: Import kind histogram for this collapsed module edge. Allowed keys: static, dynamic, require, reexport, side.

sourceRoleCounts.description: Whole-edge importer role histogram using deterministic path conventions.

importUsageCounts.description: Whole-edge import usage histogram. `value` means the import is not explicit type-only syntax; it does not claim runtime execution.

productValueCount.description: Whole-edge joint count where sourceRole=production and importUsage=value. Never derive this intersection from marginal histograms.

evidence.description: Bounded exact file-level import receipts supporting this collapsed module edge.

evidenceLimited.description: True when more file edges exist than the bounded evidence receipt includes.

packageImportEvidence.description: Root Go module-only, bounded package import evidence. It is observed static source evidence, never a runtime claim or semantic relation approval.

packageImportEvidenceSummary.description: Bounded Go package-import census. Call fullEvidenceCall to retrieve the complete typed receipt; focusReview itself contains legacy file edges only.

reconciliation.description: Module edges diffed against the vault's compiled depends_on edges (alias-normalized). null when no vault is loadable (e.g. scanning a foreign repo). Absent when reconcile:false.

inCodeMissingFromVault.description: Import-backed review candidates missing from the vault whose endpoints already exist. Each carries exact source evidence plus `rationale_review_required`; no write action is emitted.

inCodeMissingEndpointAbsent.description: Import-backed review candidates whose from/to includes a slug not yet modelled as a vault node (`absentEndpoints`). Model endpoints, inspect evidence, supply semantic rationale, and obtain human approval before any relation write.

inVaultNotInCode.description: vault depends_on edges with no matching code import — possibly stale, review before removing.

delivery.description: Present only when omitted reviewMode was automatically compacted because the estimated full MCP result exceeded the safe delivery boundary.
